newsitem.title: USA: U.S. budget negotiations to resume on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. budget negotiations to resume on Wednesday.

text.p: Negotiators for the White House and the congressional budget committees are to meet on Capitol Hill Wednesday afternoon to discuss the spending side of the budget, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said, adding there may be talks later in the day on taxes.

Speaking to reporters, McCurry declined direct comment on the tax compromise reached late Tuesday between House and Senate Republicans, saying only: "They clearly did not write the final version of tax legislation last night."

"There's already a meeting scheduled up on the hill this afternoon with members of our budget team and some of the congressional budget committee leaders to talk about the spending bill and there may even be some discussions later in the day on the tax bill as well," McCurry said.

McCurry avoided commenting on the tax compromise worked out between the House and Senate Republicans, which includes a number of provisions that the White House has previously objected to, including the indexation of capital gains.

Asked if Clinton would veto the bill as worked out between the two sides on Tuesday, McCurry said: "The bill's a long way from finished. The only thing that's happened is that the Republicans stopped fighting amongst themselves about the tax bill but they now have to sit down and negotiate with Democratic members of Congress and also with the White House. So we've got a ways to go."
